label: copy-phase input r, mid-copy (recall 3-5), not last step
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input token is r (99.3% of activation mass; in_in_first=0 always, i.e. the r is a repeat of an original r). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Position strongly gates it: rate peaks at recall_idx 3-4 (input r was original token 2-3) and in long sequences (L=8-9, t=11-13); the top activations (~4.0-4.6) are all r at original position 2 in L=9 sequences with 5 outputs remaining. It is weak or silent when the r is copied at the very last step (to_go=0), early (recall_idx<=2), or in short sequences. Output token, previous tokens and digit count have little effect. The predicate captures 96% of mass, but about 30% of predicted steps (r inputs at these positions, mostly in short sequences) stay inactive, so precision is incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: r, l, k, s, d, i; least: u, 1, 3, t) and the previous input (most: r, 0, i, 2, h, g; least: t, w, v, <DEL>); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, t=12, L=9 & t=12.
